prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1370; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision in a parking area. Insured states vehicle front bumper and hood damaged. Claimant vehicle involved; driver reports wrist injury and has retained counsel. Liability questions noted for review. Photos requested from insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office. Counsel confirmed representation and asked that all contact be routed through their office. Requested police report, medical records, and vehicle repair estimate. Scene photos received from insured and placed in file.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report. Officer noted both vehicles were slow-moving with minimal visible damage at scene. Fault determination pending witness statement. Vehicle inspection scheduled with appraiser for claimant vehicle. Medical authorization forms sent to counsel.

Entry 4: Received claimant's medical summary from counsel. Diagnosis listed as fracture of the wrist with immobilization and follow-up orthopedic care. Referred file to bodily injury review. Reserve adjusted to reflect injury exposure. Estimate for repairs under review by the appraiser.

Entry 5: Appraiser report received on claimant vehicle, damage consistent with reported impact. Counsel notified that liability is under evaluation and that a settlement position will follow review of medical bills. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days.
